en.prompt: On the unit circle $P=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ and $Q=(\cos(\theta+\pi/2),\sin(\theta+\pi/2))$. (a) Prove $\triangle OMP\cong\triangle ONQ$; (b) find $Q$; (c) state sine/cosine identities; (d) find the other four identities.

steps.title: Calculate
steps.body: (a) $OP=OQ=1$ and both triangles are right triangles. Since $\angle QOX=\theta+\pi/2$ and $\angle NOX=\pi/2$, $\angle QON=(\theta+\pi/2)-\pi/2=\theta=\angle POM$. Thus they are congruent by hypotenuse and acute angle.

steps.title: Calculate
steps.body: (b) Congruence gives $ON=OM=\cos\theta$ and $NQ=MP=\sin\theta$; $Q$ has negative x-coordinate and positive y-coordinate.

steps.title: Calculate
steps.body: (c) The x-coordinate of $Q$ is both $\cos(\theta+\pi/2)$ and $-\sin\theta$, giving $\cos(\theta+\pi/2)=-\sin\theta$. Its y-coordinate is both $\sin(\theta+\pi/2)$ and $\cos\theta$, giving $\sin(\theta+\pi/2)=\cos\theta$.

steps.title: Calculate
steps.body: (d) $\tan(\theta+\pi/2)=\cos\theta/(-\sin\theta)=-\cot\theta$; $\cot(\theta+\pi/2)=(-\sin\theta)/\cos\theta=-\tan\theta$; $\sec(\theta+\pi/2)=1/(-\sin\theta)=-\csc\theta$; $\csc(\theta+\pi/2)=1/\cos\theta=\sec\theta$. Each identity holds on its common domain where its denominators are nonzero.
